s1.syndrome_frame: Neurocutaneous disorder with seizures and multiple congenital anomalies
salient_findings: Massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
key_facts: Patient is a 12-month-old boy
Presented with convulsive seizures
Seizures characterized by faltering, smirking with withdrawal of the head and eyes
Had a blond hair strand at birth
Had polydactyly of the right hand at birth
Cardiac rhabdomyoma at birth
Depigmented spots appeared on torso at 4 months
First convulsive seizures noted at 8 months
Psychomotor development was normal for age
No family history of similar conditions
Brain CT scan showed massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
Brain MRI with contrast revealed extracranial solid mass in posterior fossa with brain stem compression
Genetic testing revealed TSC1 gene mutation

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has TSC1 gene mutation, cardiac rhabdomyoma, depigmented spots, and seizures, which are all characteristic features of TSC

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seizures and depigmented spots, which can be seen in Sturge-Weber Syndrome, although the presence of TSC1 gene mutation and other features make TSC more likely

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seizures and multiple congenital anomalies, which can be seen in NF1, although the specific features of TSC are more prominent in this case

shortlist.label: Epidermal Nevus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has depigmented spots and seizures, which can be seen in Epidermal Nevus Syndrome, although the presence of TSC1 gene mutation and other features make TSC more likely

shortlist.label: Linear Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has depigmented spots and seizures, which can be seen in Linear Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome, although the presence of TSC1 gene mutation and other features make TSC more likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of convulsive seizures, depigmented spots, polydactyly, cardiac rhabdomyoma, and brain imaging findings of tubers and subcortical lesions, along with a confirmed TSC1 gene mutation, strongly support the diagnosis of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
rejected.why: No café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, or other characteristic features

rejected.label: Epidermal Nevus Syndrome
rejected.why: No epidermal nevi or other characteristic skin lesions

rejected.label: Linear Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome
rejected.why: No linear sebaceous nevi or other characteristic skin lesions
